10.1002_adma.75317: The practical application of anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is hindered by the lack of durable anodes for industrial‐scale current densities (≥ 1000 mA cm −2 ). Herein, we report a scalable Fe 3+ ‐triggered homogeneous slow‐corrosion strategy to fabricate a Fe‐doped Ni(OH) 2 /NiS hybrid on nickel foam (Fe‐Ni(OH) 2 /NiS/NF) for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). This approach couples the slow corrosion of Ni foam by Fe 3+ with the in situ nucleation of the Fe‐Ni(OH) 2 /NiS hybrid, creating a seamless, interface‐free integration with exceptional mechanical adhesion. The optimized Fe‐Ni(OH) 2 /NiS/NF electrode exhibits exceptional stability for over 1100 h at ampere‐level current densities up to 2000 mA cm −2 without performance decay. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the catalyst undergoes rapid reconstruction at low potentials to form an amorphous Ni(Fe)OOH layer, which serves as the true active phase and primarily follows the adsorbate evolution mechanism, thereby avoiding the chemical degradation associated with lattice oxygen participation. Density functional theory calculations indicate that Fe doping upshifts the NiOOH d‐band center, strengthening * OH adsorption and thus lowering the * OH→ * O barrier to accelerate OER kinetics. In an AEMWE, it requires only 1.706 and 1.852 V to achieve 1.0 and 2.0 A cm −2 , respectively, maintaining stable operation at industrial currents for over 1800 h.
10.1016_j.est.2026.123665: Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) are extensively studied for electrochemical energy storage owing to their improved safety and mechanical stability compared to liquid electrolytes; however, electrolyte retention and long-term stability remain major challenges. In this work, a polymer-based gel electrolyte containing a conventional LiPF 6 /EC-DMC electrolyte was investigated before and after mechanical agitation in electrochemical capacitor cells. Electrochemical characterization was combined with Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) and spatial mapping to evaluate electrolyte distribution and ion–polymer interactions. The as-prepared gel exhibited homogeneous electrolyte distribution, while post-agitation analysis indicated partial electrolyte loss, reflected by reduced electrolyte-related signal intensity. Despite mechanical stress, characteristic carbonyl and PF 6 − bands remained detectable throughout the gel, confirming the retention of electrochemically active ionic species. FT-IR analysis further revealed changes in C–O–C and P–F vibrations, suggesting enhanced ion–polymer interactions after electrochemical aging. Quantitative mapping showed a 30–50% decrease in electrolyte-related band intensity after agitation while preserving continuous ionic pathways. These findings demonstrate that the investigated GPE maintains sufficient electrolyte retention and electrochemical functionality after mechanical stress, highlighting its potential as a stable quasi-solid electrolyte for mechanically robust electrochemical capacitors.

Here, we combine electrochemical fluorescence microscopy (EFM), which maps electronic connectivity by visualizing an electrofluorophore reaction distribution, with a multitask ElasticNet regression to forecast discharge capacity from spatial heterogeneity. Analyzing 196 images from six pilot-scale LiNi 0.5 Mn 0.3 Co 0.2 O 2 cathodes with varying carbon loadings, we extract 62 descriptors that capture morphology and texture. A compact five-feature model predicts capacity across eight discharge rates, achieving a per-target R 2 of up to 0.63 and an overall R 2 of 0.92, with a mean absolute percentage error of less than 2%. This performance rivals impedance-based approaches while avoiding their reliance on postformation data and incomplete electronic network information. Our facile and rapid, image-driven method may enable electrode quality control upstream of costly cell assembly to offer a transformative tool for data-driven battery research and manufacturing.

10.1109_tpel.2026.3705093: Conventional modular battery packs lack a scalable and chemistry-agnostic mechanism for replacing or reconfiguring battery modules without interrupting system operation. This letter introduces a novel seamless module-swapping strategy that enables continuous operation during both charging and discharging, independent of the number of modules per bank. The proposed method actively drives the outgoing module current to near zero before disconnection and gradually ramps up the incoming module current, achieving smooth transitions. Moreover, the proposed strategy is compatible with module-level active balancing techniques. Additional advantages are its chemistry-agnostic nature, as it only requires bus voltage and module current, and its scalability. The effectiveness of the strategy is experimentally validated under both charging and discharging modes.
